sum: Mondelez International reported third quarter 2026 sales of US$9,967 million and net income of US$1,305 million, together with a collaboration with Accenture to apply agentic AI across its Order to Cash operations.

The AI led overhaul of Order to Cash targets faster collections, lower operating friction and richer real time data, directly linking Mondelez International's commercial execution, cash generation and customer experience.
This article considers how Mondelez International's reported earnings, together with the agentic AI rollout, could influence the broader investment narrative.
Compare Mondelez International's AI driven efficiency push with other companies reshaping operations through automation. Scan our hand picked 53 AI infrastructure stocks for potential ideas.

To own Mondelez International, you need to believe its global snacking portfolio, pricing and brand investment can offset input cost swings and consumer trade downs. The analyst consensus Narrative on Simply Wall St leans on steady revenue expansion and modest margin improvement, with AI linked productivity and supply chain work aiming to keep earnings quality resilient.

The Accenture agentic AI rollout sits squarely on the short term catalyst list because it targets cash conversion, working capital and issue resolution speed. Execution risk sits on the other side. If cocoa costs or lower income demand worsen again while Mondelez International keeps spending heavily on brands and tech, earnings could feel a squeeze.

The new Order to Cash collaboration with Accenture is the clearest near term operational swing factor tied to the recent update. Management is wiring AI into customer service, supply chain and finance to improve visibility on millions of transactions, with an eye on faster collections, fewer errors and more precise decisions across the commercial engine.

Did Lotus Bakeries' 86% Run Pass You By? What The Bulls Got Right
sum: If you only glanced at Lotus Bakeries headlines during the year, the story might have looked straightforward. For Lotus Bakeries shareholders, the return over the past year was 86.3%, including dividends. Yet the starting point in November 2025 was anything but simple, with bullish voices focused on Mondelez partnerships and a Thailand plant, and skeptics worried about regulation, health trends, and Biscoff concentration. If you were weighing those arguments then, what truly tipped the scales?
A Narrative on Simply Wall St is one investor's written case for a company, with its growth, margin and multiple assumptions spelled out. Those assumptions imply an estimated Fair Value.
The shares cost €7,530 at the start of the period, and anyone eyeing Lotus Bakeries then was really choosing between two sharply different stories about where things might go next.

On the optimistic side, one Narrative saw the Mondelez partnership and the planned Thailand plant widening global reach, with a Fair Value of €9,636. That view leaned on assumed 10.2% annual revenue growth and a profit margin rising to 13.0% over three years.

The more cautious Narrative focused on regulation and health demands pressuring core products, putting Fair Value at €6,731. That case still assumed 8.3% yearly revenue growth, but flagged Biscoff concentration and rising compliance and supply chain costs as key threats.

Lotus Bakeries then announced a €500 million Biscoff expansion plan and reported H1 2026 revenue of €749.093 million and net income of €98.08 million. Net margin moved from 12.1% in H1 2025 to 13.1%. That combination, together with news of extra capacity in Belgium, Thailand and the US, largely supported the optimistic reach and profitability story, while leaving regulation worries untested.

The hinge assumption here was whether volume and margin could move together. When you assess another consumer stock, compare that claim with revenue, absolute profit and net margin in the next full reporting period.

Mondelez International stock faces new Snowballs trademark dispute
sum: Mondelez International is facing a new UK trademark dispute involving Cadbury Snowballs and Moo Free's White Choccy Snowballs. Just Food reported the development on Thursday, November 5, 2026.

Mondelez contacted Moo Free over the family-owned company's White Choccy Snowballs product. Mondelez said no legal action had been taken, that it had made Moo Free aware of its trademark rights and that it remained open to an amicable resolution.

Moo Free co-founder Mike Jessop said the company had been asked to remove the product from sale immediately. Moo Free does not accept that infringement has been established and has responded to the correspondence, according to Just Food.

The dispute adds a brand-protection test for Mondelez as the Christmas selling season approaches. Protecting Cadbury's Snowballs name may support portfolio control, while a prolonged conflict with a smaller vegan producer could create reputational pressure.

Mondelez International stock adds Undercover deal to renewed volume growth
sum: Mondel?z International reported renewed volume growth for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026, and added a portfolio transaction to its growth agenda. In its October 29 earnings release, the snack maker said organic net revenue rose 2.1%, with volume and mix contributing 1.8 percentage points and pricing adding 0.3 percentage points.

The latest development is Mondel?z's agreement to acquire Undercover Snacks, a maker of chocolate-covered and frosted quinoa crisps. The transaction broadens the company's presence in the permissible-indulgence segment and is expected to close in early 2027, subject to customary conditions and regulatory approval.

The new report also provides a fuller view of quarterly profitability. Reported diluted earnings per share increased to 1.02 US dollars, while adjusted earnings per share rose 5.5% on a constant-currency basis to 0.78 US dollars. The company attributed the adjusted improvement to operating gains and lower costs, while higher tax, interest and other expenses partly offset the benefit.

Emerging markets generated 4.1% organic growth, led by 7.7% growth in Asia, the Middle East and Africa and 6.9% growth in Latin America. Developed markets grew 0.8% organically. Europe declined 2.1% organically but delivered 1.6 percentage points of positive volume and mix, while North America grew 1.6% organically.

Management said continued investment in brands, innovation and distribution should support volume-led earnings growth. The company reaffirmed its 2026 outlook for organic net revenue growth of at least 2%, adjusted earnings per share growth of flat to 5% on a constant-currency basis and free cash flow of approximately 3 billion US dollars.
The real-time quote of Mondelez International stock was 58.53 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 16:30 CET on Monday, November 2, 2026.
For investors, the key question is whether renewed volume momentum can persist while the company absorbs ongoing commodity, trade and consumer-spending volatility.

sum: Mondel?z International enters the week with investors weighing a stronger volume trend against a still cautious cost environment. The company reported third-quarter 2026 results on Thursday, October 29, and management kept its 2026 revenue and earnings outlook unchanged.

Quarterly revenue reached 9.967 billion US dollars, while diluted earnings per share came to 1.02 US dollars. The earnings release and conference-call schedule were published by Mondel?z International. The earnings-call summary showed adjusted earnings per share of 0.78 US dollars against a 0.72 US dollar estimate, while revenue was slightly below the consensus estimate.

Management said emerging markets continued to support volume and top-line growth. It also pointed to improving conditions in Europe, continued momentum in North America and productivity savings as supports for strong earnings-per-share growth in 2027.

The expansion opportunity remains material in China, India and Brazil. Management estimates that roughly 25 percent of additional numeric distribution remains available across those markets, although the company also expects to reinvest part of its third-quarter upside in innovation, advertising and commercialization.

Mondelez Q1 Earnings Beat Estimates, Revenues Up 8.2% Y/Y
sum: Mondelez International, Inc. MDLZ posted first-quarter 2026 results, wherein both top and bottom lines beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate. While net sales increased, earnings decreased from the year-ago period's actuals.

Adjusted earnings were 67 cents per share, which decreased 14.9% on a constant-currency (cc) basis. The decline was caused by weaker operating performance and higher income taxes, partially offset by lower interest and other expenses, as well as a reduced share count. The metric beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate of 61 cents per share.
Mondelez International, Inc. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise
Mondelez International, Inc. price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Mondelez International, Inc. Quote

Net revenues rose 8.2% year over year to $10,080 million, outpacing the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $9,790 million. This growth was driven by favorable currency-related factors and underlying organic net revenue gains, partially offset by the absence of prior-year revenues from a divestiture.
Organic net revenues rose 3% year over year in the first quarter, primarily driven by pricing, which contributed 3.5 percentage points, while volume/mix declined 0.5 percentage points.

Revenues from emerging markets increased 11.4% year over year to $4,149 million, with organic growth of 6.3%. Growth in these markets was supported by strong results in India and Brazil, along with solid growth in China and Southeast Asia. These gains reflect continued focus on expanding distribution and strengthening consumer engagement.

Mondelez International (MDLZ) moved higher this week as investors waited for Q1 results after the market close on April 28. The stock traded near $58, still below its 52-week high of $71. The tone is cautious because investors want to see whether snack demand can stabilize.

The main issue is cocoa inflation. Mondelez raised prices to offset higher cocoa costs, but Reuters reported that consumers have pushed back, especially in the U.S. That has pressured volumes as shoppers look for cheaper options.

Q4 showed the tradeoff clearly. Revenue rose 9.3% to $10.5 billion, but pricing added 9 points while volume/mix declined 4.8 percentage points. That means sales growth was driven more by price than by selling more snacks.

Management expects 2026 organic revenue growth of flat to 2% and adjusted EPS growth of flat to 5%. That is a muted outlook for a company with global brands like Oreo, Cadbury, Ritz, and Toblerone. Going forward, the stock will likely depend on whether Q1 shows better volumes without more margin pressure.

The Hershey Company (HSY) Partners With Lindt, Mars, Mondelez, Nestlé on TogetherCocoa
sum: We recently compiled a list of the 12 Top Performing Consumer Staples Stocks in February. The Hershey Company (NYSE:HSY) is one of the best performing stocks.
TheFly reported on February 24 that Mizuho increased its price target for HSY from $165 to $195 while retaining a Neutral rating on the stock.

Recently, on February 23, The Hershey Company (NYSE:HSY) declared its involvement in the establishment of TogetherCocoa, a brand-new organization founded in partnership with Lindt & Sprüngli, Mars Incorporated, Mondelēz International, and Nestlé. The goal of this program is to assist communities that grow cocoa while encouraging industry collaboration to improve the sustainability and resilience of the world's cocoa supply chain.

TogetherCocoa provides a structured strategy to improve livelihoods while fostering industry-wide collaboration, building on long-term work to solve the living income gap for cocoa farmers in Ghana and Côte d'Ivoire. To make sure the foundation's initiatives are successful and significant, HSY underlined that it is collaborating closely with the governments of both nations, supply-chain partners, and other cocoa industry players.

Despite the fact that TogetherCocoa is still in its infancy, HSY promised to offer updates as the foundation's initiatives advance. Additionally, the company confirmed its continued dedication to its current cocoa sustainability projects, children's well-being programs, and farmer professional development, all while keeping a steady focus on helping the people and communities who are the backbone of cocoa production.
The Hershey Company (NYSE:HSY) is a U.S. manufacturer and marketer of chocolate, confectionery, and snack products, distributing globally through retail, e-commerce, and foodservice channels.

items.t: Sugar, stocks and scrutiny: Mondelez, Kraft and General Mills caught in Trump’s nutrition reset
sum: - The Trump administration’s new dietary guidelines mark a tougher stance on sugar and ultra-processed foods (UPFs), unsettling major packaged food companies whose portfolios are heavily built around those categories.

- While no immediate regulations were announced, the guidelines’ influence over federal food programs like school meals and SNAP raises the risk of longer-term demand shifts for core packaged food products.
- The baking industry is pushing back early, arguing that staple grain foods remain affordable, nutritious and essential to the US food system as policy discussions move forward.

Dietary guidelines rarely move markets. They’re updated every five years, debated by nutrition experts and generally absorbed without much fuss by the food industry. For most companies, they shape public messaging rather than day-to-day business decisions.

That pattern broke this week. When the Trump administration released its 2025-2030 Dietary Guidelines, shares in several major packaged food companies fell, even as the broader market stayed relatively steady. Those that felt it most were the CPG majors most closely associated with sugar-heavy, refined and ultra-processed foods.

The reaction wasn’t driven by a single recommendation, but by how the document reads as a whole. Added sugar is no longer treated as something to manage carefully. Highly processed foods are called out directly. Protein, fats and whole foods are elevated in ways that quietly downgrade many familiar packaged categories.

At a White House briefing, Health Secretary Robert F Kennedy Jr framed the reset as a break from decades of federal nutrition policy, accusing previous administrations of prioritizing corporate interests over public health. No new regulations were announced, but the language marked a clear shift from the more cautious phrasing the industry has grown used to.
